entries.name: Downy mildew
entries.pathogen: oomycete water moulds, not true fungi
symptoms: grey fuzzy or downy growth on the underside of the leaf
yellow angular spots on the upper leaf surface, bounded by the veins
the upper surface can look quilted
leaves become brittle and misshapen
in severe cases leaves and flowers drop
confusions: powdery mildew leaves a white powder usually on the upper surface, downy mildew is grey fuzz underneath
nutrient deficiency yellows evenly and does not produce fuzz on the underside
early blight has brown spots with concentric rings and no underside fuzz
entries.conditions: favoured by crowded plants and wet leaf undersides that do not dry. Spreads fast in moist conditions and can cause total crop loss within weeks.
treatment: space plants so leaves dry and air moves through
water at the base, keep the leaf undersides dry, drip is better than overhead
remove and destroy affected leaves and plants
many standard fungicides do not work, downy mildews are not true fungi, use a product labelled for downy mildew and follow the label
avoid working in the plot when the leaves are wet, you spread the spores

entries.name: Spider mites
entries.pathogen: Tetranychus species, especially two spotted spider mite
symptoms: tiny white or yellow speckles on the leaves, called stippling
leaves look faded, dry or sandblasted despite watering
fine silk webbing on the underside of leaves and between stems
leaves take on a bronze colour as feeding continues
severe attack turns whole leaves yellow and they drop
confusions: aphids are visible and leave honeydew, mites are tiny and leave webbing
leafminer damage is hollow mines inside the leaf, not surface speckling
nutrient deficiency does not produce webbing
entries.conditions: mites are tiny, you usually notice the damage before the pest. They feed on the undersides and thrive in hot dry conditions. Dusty leaves make them worse.
treatment: check the undersides with a hand lens, or shake leaves over white paper and watch for moving specks
spray the leaf undersides with a strong jet of water to knock them back
use insecticidal soap or neem oil, cover the undersides where the mites live
keep plants well watered, drought stressed plants suffer more
avoid dusty conditions and excessive nitrogen which favours them
spare natural predators, they often keep mites in check

entries.name: Fall armyworm
symptoms: window pane damage on young leaves, clear patches where the surface is scraped
ragged, irregular holes in leaves as caterpillars grow
sawdust like frass in the whorl, tassels and cobs
caterpillar with a pale upside down Y on the head
four raised spots in a trapezium on each body segment
four spots in a square on the second to last segment
skin smooth to the touch
confusions: cotton bollworm has similar dots but a paler head and feels rough with tiny spines
African armyworm and stem borers also feed on maize but lack the Y mark and dot pattern
entries.conditions: larvae develop between 11C and 30C, optimum 28C. Heavy rain washes eggs and young larvae off leaves.
treatment: scout early, check the newest two or three leaves in the funnel where moths lay and larvae feed
handpick and crush egg masses and small larvae on small plots
apply wood ash, sand, or dry soil into the whorl on small plots
encourage natural enemies, ants are important predators, avoid broad spectrum sprays that kill them
neem and hot pepper extracts applied to the whorl are used with reported success
if spraying, aim the nozzle into the whorl, spray early morning or late afternoon, and rotate pesticide groups

entries.name: Bacterial wilt
symptoms: youngest leaves wilt during the heat of the day and seem to recover overnight
wilting spreads to the whole plant while the leaves stay green
cut a stem crosswise, it looks brown and a milky or yellowish ooze may be visible
brown streaks in the vascular tissue along a split stem
eventual complete collapse of the plant
confusions: Fusarium wilt gives one sided yellowing or wilting
Verticillium wilt gives V shaped lesions on the leaflets
Southern blight has white strands at the soil line and small round tan bodies
entries.conditions: favoured by high temperature and high moisture. The bacterium survives in soil for years and enters through root wounds from transplanting, cultivation or insects.
treatment: there is no chemical control for bacterial wilt
remove and destroy infected plants, do not leave them in the plot
rotate away from tomato, pepper, eggplant, potato and sunflower for at least three years, use maize, beans or cabbage instead
plant certified disease free seedlings
disinfect tools and boots that touched infested soil before moving to another plot
grafted tomatoes on resistant rootstock give the strongest control where available

entries.name: Early blight
symptoms: small brown lesions first on the older lower leaves
spots enlarge with concentric rings in a bullseye pattern
tissue around the spots turns yellow
stem lesions can girdle the plant near the soil line
fruit lesions are large with concentric rings, infected fruit often drops
confusions: late blight lesions are dark and water soaked with white mould on the leaf underside
bacterial spot lesions are smaller and angular
entries.conditions: the fungus survives on infected debris in the soil, on seed, and on volunteer tomato plants. High temperature and humidity after the lesions appear kills foliage fast.
treatment: remove and destroy infected lower leaves and branches
mulch to stop soil splash, water at the base, keep foliage dry
space plants so they do not touch
rotate and clear volunteer tomato and nightshade weeds
maintain potassium and calcium, side dress with calcium nitrate
if severe, mancozeb is very effective, copper or chlorothalonil are good, follow the label

entries.name: Tomato leafminer
symptoms: blotch shaped mines in the leaves, the most distinctive sign
larvae inside the leaf tissue and later inside the fruit
leaf curling and drying under heavy attack
stunted growth, damaged flowers and fruits
small cream eggs laid near the leaf veins and stems
confusions: leafminer flies make narrow winding mines, Tuta makes blotch mines
early blight lesions are fungal spots, not hollowed mines
entries.conditions: a single female lays up to 300 eggs. Yield loss can reach 100 percent if unmanaged. This pest caused tomato shortages in Nigeria.
treatment: inspect the crop weekly for the first mines and remove infested leaves
mass trap moths with pheromone sticky traps, 20 to 40 traps per hectare, start when traps catch more than three or four moths a week
remove and destroy crop debris after harvest, do not leave it beside the field
rotate insecticide groups because Tuta develops resistance quickly
netting or screens on nursery and high value plots
avoid continuous tomato on the same land

entries.name: Cassava mosaic disease
entries.pathogen: African cassava mosaic virus complex, begomoviruses
symptoms: irregular yellow or yellow green mosaic on the leaves
misshapen and twisted leaflets
leaf distortion and vein clearing
stunted growth overall
few or no tubers on badly affected plants
confusions: cassava bacterial blight gives angular water soaked leaf spots and gum exudate, not mosaic
nutrient deficiency yellows more evenly without leaf twisting
entries.conditions: spread by infected stem cuttings used as planting material, and by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Yield loss ranges from 32 to 69 percent.
treatment: use certified disease free cuttings, this is the single most important step
plant resistant varieties, IITA bred lines such as TMS 30572 and related releases are widely available in Nigeria
uproot and destroy badly affected plants early, do not take cuttings from them
control whitefly and remove weeds that harbour the virus
do not move cuttings from a diseased plot to a clean one
interplant resistant with local landraces to reduce spread

entries.name: Groundnut rosette disease
entries.pathogen: Groundnut rosette virus complex with its assistor virus and satellite RNA
symptoms: severely stunted plants with bunched, rosette shaped growth
chlorotic rosette: leaves turn yellow or yellow green and mottle
green rosette: leaves stay green but are small and bunched
little or no pod set on affected plants
confusions: leaf spot diseases give distinct brown or black spots on leaves
aphid damage alone stunts but does not make the rosette growth form
entries.conditions: transmitted by the groundnut aphid Aphis craccivora. Aphids need a long feed to acquire the virus, which gives a window to act. Found only in sub Saharan Africa, the vector is worldwide.
treatment: sow early in the season so plants mature before aphid numbers peak
sow at recommended density, dense cover leaves fewer bare patches that guide aphids in
spray insecticide between germination and day 40 to cut aphid spread
plant resistant varieties where available
intercrop with pigeon pea, maize or sorghum to interfere with aphid movement
remove volunteer and diseased groundnut plants and weeds that harbour aphids

entries.name: Cowpea aphid borne mosaic
entries.pathogen: Cowpea aphid borne mosaic virus and related viruses
symptoms: mosaic mottling on the leaves, light and dark green patches
leaf distortion and reduced leaf size
stunted plants
poor pod and grain formation
confusions: aphid colonies alone cause curling and honeydew but not true mosaic
nutrient deficiency does not distort the leaf shape this way
entries.conditions: spread by aphids and is also seedborne. Known in Nigeria since 1976 as a serious legume virus in all agro ecological zones.
treatment: use certified or virus free seed, the virus is seedborne
remove weeds that harbour aphids
control aphids early with insecticide, do not wait for colonies to build
rouge out badly affected plants
plant resistant varieties where available
avoid planting cowpea next to an old infected field

entries.name: Okra yellow vein mosaic
entries.pathogen: Bhendi yellow vein mosaic virus, begomovirus
symptoms: yellowing of the leaf veins, which spreads to the whole leaf
leaf curling
stunted growth
poor flowering and small deformed pods
confusions: nutrient yellowing starts between the veins, mosaic starts on the veins
powdery mildew leaves a white powder, not vein yellowing
entries.conditions: transmitted by whitefly. It is the major limitation on okra production. First described in 1924 in Bombay and now widespread.
treatment: control whitefly, this is the main lever
remove and destroy infected plants early
keep the field weed free, weeds harbour whitefly
intercrop with maize or marigold to reduce whitefly landing
plant tolerant varieties where available
do not save seed from affected plants

entries.name: Striga (witchweed)
symptoms: stunted, yellow, scorched looking plants, easily mistaken for drought stress
wilting despite adequate moisture
small purple or pink flowers at ground level around the base of the crop
the parasite is attached to the crop roots underground before any visible sign
confusions: drought stress looks similar above ground but the soil is dry and there are no Striga flowers
nitrogen deficiency yellows evenly and responds to fertiliser
entries.conditions: Striga parasitises maize, sorghum, millet, sugarcane, upland rice and wild grasses. It attaches to the host roots and takes water and nutrients. Seeds stay viable in soil for years.
treatment: rotate with a non host trap crop such as cowpea or groundnut, they trigger Striga seeds to germinate with nothing to parasitise
hand pull Striga before it flowers, and do it before seed set or you add years of seed to the soil
apply nitrogen, a well fed crop tolerates Striga better
use improved Striga resistant cereal varieties where available
intercrop cereals with legumes to reduce Striga emergence
there are herbicide seed treatment options for sorghum and millet
